beats.role_note: COLD OPEN / walker B00 — ClaudeComposerAsk. Illustrative reconstruction, not a transcript.
beats.narration_text: Merhaba, this is Liam, in for Bear. Today we take apart assignment three of Tin Knockout, Tharun Maheswararao's game about tin wind-up toys boxing in an empty goldfish bowl. This time the game gets three 3D props, built in Blender and checked in Godot. The prompt on screen is an illustrative reconstruction, not a saved transcript.

beats.narration_text: Here is the real engine render of the prop room, all three props on its floor. Everything is sized against Bolt, one point eight metres tall. The castle is the sunken-castle ornament, the landmark that says goldfish bowl, at two point three metres. The windkey is a spare brass winding key, a collectible that would refill Bolt's spring. The toy box is where weapon pickups would come from. Its lid sits at Bolt's waist.

beats.role_note: The A3 brief (3ef263b) committed before any building; what it fixes; its predicted failures.
beats.narration_text: The brief came first. Commit three e f two six three adds it before the first build commit. Tharun chose the three assets and the scale. Claude drafted the numbers, colours and failure cases, and Tharun accepted them unchanged. It fixes what the checks test later: size within one centimetre, the base at zero, triangle budgets, and which way the front faces. And it predicts seven ways this could go wrong.

beats.role_note: Setup frictions from FRICTIONAL.md (A3), with the student's own connected screenshot.
beats.narration_text: Setup took three fixes, all logged. The chapter's claude m c p add line failed: dash e takes several values, so it swallowed the server name. Install add-on failed until Blender had been opened once. Enabling the add-on needed a full Blender restart. Then this, Tharun's own screenshot: connected on port nine eight seven six, which Claude found bound to one two seven dot zero dot zero dot one only. Even so, the first get scene info call said, could not connect to Blender. Four minutes later, it worked.

props.source: Godot editor reconstruction · godot/tests/check_props3d.gd lines 83–90 at 1d93dcb, verbatim

var diff: Vector3 = (box.size - (spec.size as Vector3)).abs()
		check(diff.x <= TOL and diff.y <= TOL and diff.z <= TOL,
			"size %s matches brief %s within %.2f m" % [box.size, spec.size, TOL])
		check(absf(box.position.y) <= 0.005, "base at y=0 (min_y %.4f)" % box.position.y)
		check(inst.scale.is_equal_approx(Vector3.ONE) and nodes_ok, "scale (1,1,1) and rotation 0 on scene and mesh nodes")
		if spec.tall_axis != "":
			check(box.size.y >= box.size.x and box.size.y >= box.size.z, "tallest axis is Y (stands upright)")
		check(tris <= spec.budget, "triangles %d <= budget %d" % [tris, spec.budget])

beats.role_note: Code: check_props3d.gd lines 30–40 — the to_root() fix and the comment recording the false pass.
beats.narration_text: What Claude got wrong. The comment on lines thirty to thirty-three records it. Claude's first version of this check read global transform on props that were not yet inside the scene tree. Godot logged an error and returned the identity. Line thirty-four is the fix. To root builds the transform from local transforms, parent by parent, which works before the node is in the tree.

show.event: line 31: the comment records the false pass
line 38: parent by parent, local transforms

props.title: What Claude Got Wrong: the Room Check
props.source: Godot editor reconstruction · godot/tests/check_props3d.gd lines 30–40 at 1d93dcb, verbatim
props.code:
# Transform of n relative to the scene root, built from local transforms so it
# works before the node is inside the tree (global_transform does not: a first
# version of this check used it, got the identity, and "passed" the room check
# without testing placement at all).
func to_root(n: Node) -> Transform3D:
	var t := Transform3D.IDENTITY
	while n != null and n != root:
		if n is Node3D:
			t = (n as Node3D).transform * t
		n = n.get_parent()
	return t

beats.role_note: YOUR TURN — a useful Walker prompt read aloud, one bounded change + prediction, human/AI credits (SOURCES.md "Assignment 3"), revision; Liam signs off before the locked outro.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here is a useful Walker prompt. Please use Walker to add one check to check props 3 d dot g d that compares every surface's albedo with the hex colours in the change brief, and tell me which surface you predict will fail before you run it. My prediction: the toy box band, because the brief still says navy and the hand edit made it green. Then a person decides: revise the brief, or revert the edit. Credits, plainly. Claude wrote all the Blender code, the Godot scene and check, and the docs. Tharun chose the assets and the scale, reviewed and accepted the brief, learned the window and took the screenshots, ran and approved the M C P sessions, made the hand edit, and did the look check. This voice is Kokoro text to speech. The source shown is revision one d nine three d c b. Liam, in for Bear.
